A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MP-HSIR and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary materials. Content can be matched despite renumbering and erroneous cross-references in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original restoration benchmarks, generalization experiments, real-world visual results, and module ablations in Section 4 and the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds real-world quality scores, inference timings, and a sequential restoration example.

M1.justification: v2 adds a sequential inference extension: denoising, then deblurring, then dehazing under successive prompt guidance (Appendix J.4, Figure 9). v1 demonstrates selective removal without this sequence. The underlying architecture, prompt components, losses, and training procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The 13 datasets and nine restoration tasks are retained. v2 Figure 9 adds a combined noise, blur, and haze scenario requiring sequential removal, extending v1's controllability examples involving noise plus blur. The new Urban and EO-1 scores use existing dataset coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds explicit comparisons with AirNet, PromptIR, HAIR, InstructIR, and PromptHSI within the controllability analysis (Figure 9); v1's controllability examples show only MP-HSIR. Comparator membership in the retained benchmark tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 introduces no-reference QSFL evaluation on Urban and EO-1 and an inference-time comparison using 64 x 64 x 100 remote sensing inputs (Tables 10 and 15). Existing splits, degradation settings, training budgets, and PSNR/SSIM evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 9 tests whether prompt-guided restoration can remove multiple degradations sequentially, extending the earlier selective-removal case studies. The efficiency analysis also gains measured latency. Existing module ablations, spectral-prompt visualizations, and two-degradation examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for restoration results. The added average inference times do not introduce uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Retained benchmark, classifier, complexity, and ablation values are unchanged. v2 adds MP-HSIR QSFL scores of 11.42 on Urban and 16.54 on EO-1 (Table 10), inference time of 0.083 seconds (Table 15), and sequential PSNR values of 18.01, 19.16, and 30.12 dB (Figure 9). These are new results, not improvements over corresponding v1 measurements.

T1.justification: Equations 1–12 and their mathematical content, including attention operations, predictor loss, and degradation synthesis, are retained. v2 introduces no new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about tri-modal prompts, spectral reconstruction, controllability, and performance across nine restoration tasks. The additional appendix evidence does not redefine the core contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix J newly interprets the added evaluations as evidence of practical generalization, a favorable efficiency–accuracy tradeoff, suitability for large-scale deployment, and flexible sequential restoration. v1 discusses complexity and selective restoration without these additional interpretations.

D1.justification: The abstract changes the code and models from a promised future release to reported availability. Existing implementation and training disclosures are retained. The new timing comparison specifies input dimensions but provides no hardware details.

R1.justification: v2 adds SPIRE by Qi et al. to the VLM restoration discussion and Yang et al.'s no-reference hyperspectral quality-assessment work for QSFL. The broader related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged; SPIRE is not added as an evaluated baseline.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited grammar and author-header edits and relabels appendices A–E as F–J. Most prose and organization are retained. It also introduces incorrect figure references, such as citing Figure 11 for the architecture still displayed as Figure 3, while leaving main-text appendix pointers unupdated.

P2.justification: v2 adds two small tables and the sequential-restoration Figure 9, adds residual-map insets to Figure 4, labels the global/local branches in Figure 3, and corrects the radar-chart method name. Existing supplementary tables and figures are largely relocated or renumbered, with a more compact final-page arrangement.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's visual-only real-world evaluation and parameter/FLOP comparison, v2 adds quantitative real-world assessment, measured latency, and sequential-restoration evidence. These modestly strengthen practical evaluation, while clearer residual displays and reported code/model availability help readers. Missing timing hardware and detailed protocols, together with widespread incorrect cross-references, limit the overall benefit.
